CHARLOTTE-AREA INDEPENDENT SCHOOLS · FINANCIAL AID & TUITION
What It Costs to Attend
Davidson Day School
A parent-facing research report on published tuition, the full cost of attendance, and
what the school discloses about tuition assistance.
Figures cover the 2026–27 school year
Prepared July 2026
Three things to know before you read.
1. Where a figure is not published, we say so. Independent schools vary widely in what cost and aid information
they put on the public record. Where Davidson Day does not publish something, we mark it a transparency gap. An
unpublished number is a gap in what the school discloses — it is never, on its own, a verdict about the school’s
quality or about how far its aid reaches.
2. Tuition and aid figures change every year. Every dollar figure and percentage in this report carries the school
year or fiscal year it applies to. Figures were retrieved in July 2026. Before making any decision, confirm current
numbers directly with the school’s business or admission office.
3. This report is about K–12 tuition assistance, not college financial aid. Davidson Day’s own aid program helps
families pay to attend the school. That is a different subject from FAFSA, the CSS Profile, and the college aid process
students face at graduation. The two are easy to confuse and are not related here.
This report describes published prices and names gaps. It does not advise any family on what it can spend or on aid
strategy, and it does not calculate what any particular family would pay.
Davidson Day School — Financial Aid & Tuition Deep Dive Report
How complete is this report?
Section-by-section confidence, based on what Davidson Day publishes.
Each section below was scored on how much of its subject the school actually puts on the public record. A low
score means the school publishes little on that topic — not that the school performs poorly on it. The pattern here is
common among independent schools: prices are published, aid statistics are not.
Section Subject Confidence
1 Tuition by grade level 90%
2 Fees and additional costs 70%
3 Aid process and timeline 85%
4 Aid reach and award size 30%
5 Merit, scholarships and discounts 78%
6 Payment plans and contract terms 55%
7 Trend and open questions 50%
The single largest gap is Section 4. Davidson Day publishes no percentage of students receiving aid, no aid budget,
and no average or median award. It does publish one unusual and concrete figure — an award ceiling — which is
covered there.
All figures apply to the 2026–27 school year unless otherwise tagged. Confirm current figures with the school’s business office. 2
Davidson Day School — Financial Aid & Tuition Deep Dive Report
SECTION 1 OF 7
The Tuition Table
What Davidson Day charges, by division, for the 2026–27 school year.
AT A GLANCE
Published range $22,590 to $26,910 for 2026–27, depending on division
How it is published Four division bands covering ages two through 12th grade
Lowest band Early Childhood, $22,590 (2026–27)
Highest band Upper School, $26,910 (2026–27)
Not published Half-day options, new-student versus returning rates, what tuition includes
Davidson Day publishes a complete current-year tuition table on its Tuition and Affordability page. The school
enrolls students from two years old through 12th grade, and the four published bands cover that entire span.
Division Grades covered 2026–27 tuition
Early Childhood Two-year-olds through Junior Kindergarten $22,590
Lower School Kindergarten through 4th grade $25,010
Middle School 5th through 8th grade $26,320
Upper School 9th through 12th grade $26,910
Read this as bands, not grades. The school prices by division rather than by individual grade, so a 1st-grader and
a 4th-grader pay the same published Lower School figure for 2026–27. There is no separate published rate for any
single grade.
The spread between the lowest and highest bands is $4,320 for 2026–27 — that is our arithmetic on the two
published figures above, not a school-published figure.
TRANSPARENCY GAP — What tuition actually includes
The tuition page does not state what tuition covers. The separate fee list (Section 2) shows that textbooks and technology
are billed on top of tuition for 7th through 12th grade, and that field experiences carry their own charge from 4th grade up,
so those are not included. Whether tuition covers lunch, athletics participation, or arts materials is not stated either way.
This is the most consequential unpublished item in this section.
TRANSPARENCY GAP — Early Childhood variants and enrollment-status pricing
Davidson Day enrolls children from age two, and programmes for this age group commonly offer half-day, part-week, or
full-day options at different prices. The published table shows a single Early Childhood figure of $22,590 for 2026–27 with
no variants listed. The school also does not publish whether new and returning students pay different rates.
Source. davidsonday.org Tuition and Affordability page (published 9 April 2026), retrieved 22 July 2026.
All figures apply to the 2026–27 school year unless otherwise tagged. Confirm current figures with the school’s business office. 3
Davidson Day School — Financial Aid & Tuition Deep Dive Report
SECTION 2 OF 7
Beyond Tuition
The published fee schedule, and the costs the school confirms exist but does not price.
AT A GLANCE
Published fee lines Five, on the same page as tuition — more than many schools publish
Largest published fee Textbooks, $300 to $1,000 for 7th–12th grade (2026–27)
Percentage-based fee Refund Plan, 2.8% of tuition (2026–27); mandatory or optional not stated
Deposit $2,400 per student for 2022–23; the current amount is not published
Confirmed but unpriced Extended care, lunch, athletics team packs, arts materials, summer programmes
The published fee schedule
Fee Applies to 2026–27 amount
Refund Plan fee Not stated 2.8% of tuition
Yearbook Not stated $75
Technology 7th through 12th grade $500
Field Experience 4th through 12th grade $500 to $1,000
Textbooks 7th through 12th grade $300 to $1,000
Two further published prices sit outside that table. Applying for tuition assistance costs $60, paid to the Clarity
platform when the application is submitted (2025–26 cycle guide). The school also runs a vintage uniform sale at $5
per item.
Costs the school confirms exist but does not price
Several costs are documented in the school’s own materials without a figure attached. Notably, the financial aid
page states that aid does not cover extended care, arts and music supplies or instruments, or athletic equipment
and team packs — which confirms these are real charges families face, while leaving the amounts unpublished.
• Extended care. Before-school care runs 7:15 to 7:40 a.m. and after-school care 2:45 to 6:00 p.m., for
Traditional Toddlers through 8th grade, at roughly a seven-to-one student-to-staff ratio. No price is published.
• Lunch. Families may order catered hot lunches from several vendors. Prices sit in a separate ordering
document rather than on the public site.
• Athletics. Team packs and athletic equipment are referred to in the aid exclusions. No participation fee or
team pack price is published.
• Arts and music. Supplies and instruments are named in the same exclusion. No price list is published.
• Summer programmes. The school runs themed summer camps. No prices appear on the school’s own
summer pages.
All figures apply to the 2026–27 school year unless otherwise tagged. Confirm current figures with the school’s business office. 4
Davidson Day School — Financial Aid & Tuition Deep Dive Report
• Admission application fee. No amount is published; applications run through the school’s family portal.
Uniforms and transportation
Uniforms are required, with Early Preschool exempt. Families buy from general retailers and have the school logo
applied by a Cornelius-based promotional vendor, or order through a national retailer’s school programme. Garment
prices are set by those vendors and are not published by the school as a fee. Spirit wear is optional. On
transportation, no school-provided busing or transportation charge was found published — which most likely means
none is offered rather than that a price is being withheld.
TRANSPARENCY GAP — The current enrollment deposit
The school’s deposit instructions for 2022–23 state a deposit of $2,400 per student. For current years the school states
only that the deposit amount appears inside each family’s Enrollment Tuition Contract, which sits behind the family portal.
The deposit is drafted immediately by bank transfer once the contract is signed. The current figure is not on the public
record.
TRANSPARENCY GAP — Why this report contains no total cost estimate
Our standing practice is to assemble published line items into an all-in annual cost range so parents can see a floor and a
realistic figure. That is not possible here. Of roughly a dozen cost components, only five carry published prices, and at
least seven more are confirmed to exist without one — including the current deposit and every recurring charge for care,
meals, athletics and arts. A range built mostly from missing parts would look authoritative and mislead, so we have not
built one. The published lines above are complete as far as they go.
Sources. davidsonday.org Tuition and Affordability page (published 9 April 2026), retrieved 22 July 2026; davidsonday.org deposit
instructions, enrollment instructions, extended care and back-to-school pages, retrieved 22 July 2026.
All figures apply to the 2026–27 school year unless otherwise tagged. Confirm current figures with the school’s business office. 5
Davidson Day School — Financial Aid & Tuition Deep Dive Report
SECTION 3 OF 7
The Aid Engine
How Davidson Day’s tuition assistance process works, and when it happens.
AT A GLANCE
Platform Clarity Financial Aid; a $60 fee is charged on submission
Deadline 15 February each year; late applications processed if funds remain
Renewal Families must reapply every year
Decisions Committee meets in early March, then on a rolling basis
How you learn The award appears inside the Enrollment Tuition Contract
Confidentiality Administered in confidence; families asked to keep awards private
Davidson Day documents its aid process in more detail than it documents its aid outcomes. The mechanics below
are all published.
The steps
• Create a Clarity account. All families create a new account the first time they use the system.
• Complete the application. Families submit a Form 4506c, which lets Clarity pull the prior year’s tax returns
directly rather than requiring uploads. There is a $60 fee to submit.
• Committee review. A Financial Aid Committee meets in early March and then on a rolling basis, working from
qualification guidance supplied by Clarity.
• Contract. The award is included in the Enrollment Tuition Contract when it is issued. Families are asked to
review and sign within two weeks of receipt.
Rules families ask about
• Both parents must file. Separated and divorced parents are each expected to complete a Clarity application
and supply tax returns. The only stated exception is a divorce agreement assigning sole responsibility for
educational expenses to one parent.
• Aid is not a loan. The school states plainly that aid is an award and is not repaid.
• Aid does not cover everything. Extended care, arts and music supplies or instruments, and athletic
equipment and team packs fall outside an award.
• Reapplication is annual. There is no multi-year award; the 15 February deadline recurs every year.
TRANSPARENCY GAP — Does applying for aid affect an admission decision?
Davidson Day does not state whether admission decisions are made without reference to a family’s aid application
(need-blind), with reference to it (need-aware), or on some other basis. This is among the most common questions
families have, and the school takes no public position either way. It is a direct question worth putting to the admission
office.
All figures apply to the 2026–27 school year unless otherwise tagged. Confirm current figures with the school’s business office. 6
Davidson Day School — Financial Aid & Tuition Deep Dive Report
TRANSPARENCY GAP — Appeals and mid-year changes
No appeals or reconsideration process is published, and no policy is published for families whose circumstances change
mid-year. The Clarity application does allow families to describe short-term financial difficulty, but what happens after an
award is issued is not documented. The composition of the Financial Aid Committee is also not published on the current
page.
Source. davidsonday.org Tuition and Affordability page (published 9 April 2026), retrieved 22 July 2026; Clarity family application
guide (2025–26), retrieved 22 July 2026.
All figures apply to the 2026–27 school year unless otherwise tagged. Confirm current figures with the school’s business office. 7
Davidson Day School — Financial Aid & Tuition Deep Dive Report
SECTION 4 OF 7
The Aid Numbers
What Davidson Day discloses about how far its aid reaches — and what it does not.
AT A GLANCE
Published award ceiling Maximum-award families pay $3,000 per student per year (2026–27)
Full-tuition awards The school states no award covers full tuition
Share of students on aid Not published
Total aid budget Not published
Average award Not published
Median award Not published
Award range Not published
Families assisted Not published
This is the thinnest section of the report, and the reason is straightforward: Davidson Day describes its aid
programme as administered in the strictest confidence, and publishes no statistics about it. What follows is
everything on the public record.
The one number the school does publish
Davidson Day states that no financial aid award covers the full cost of tuition, and that families receiving the
maximum award are required to pay $3,000 per year, per student (2026–27). It adds that some fees are not covered
by aid awards.
This is an unusual disclosure. Most independent schools publish nothing about the upper limit of an award. A family
can take the $3,000 figure as a published floor on what attendance costs in the most-assisted case — before the
unpriced fees in Section 2, which aid does not cover.
Division 2026–27 Paid by a maximum-award Implied ceiling on the award
tuition family
Early Childhood $22,590 $3,000 $19,590
Lower School $25,010 $3,000 $22,010
Middle School $26,320 $3,000 $23,320
Upper School $26,910 $3,000 $23,910
The final column is our arithmetic, subtracting the school’s published $3,000 maximum-award payment from its
published 2026–27 tuition. It is not a school-published figure. It describes only the maximum-award case and says
nothing about what a typical award looks like — the school publishes no typical award, and awards below the
maximum are presumably smaller by an unknown amount.
All figures apply to the 2026–27 school year unless otherwise tagged. Confirm current figures with the school’s business office. 8
Davidson Day School — Financial Aid & Tuition Deep Dive Report
TRANSPARENCY GAP — The statistics that would tell you how far aid reaches
Davidson Day publishes none of the following: the share of students receiving need-based aid, the total annual aid
budget, the average award, the median award, the range from smallest to largest award, the number of students or
families assisted, or how much of the aid programme is funded by endowment rather than operating budget. Without
these, it is not possible to say how many families the programme reaches or what a typical award looks like. These are
fair questions to put to the admission office directly.
A tax-filing figure, and why we are cautious about it
Davidson Day is a registered non-profit and files an annual IRS Form 990, which is a public document. Form 990
includes a line for grants and assistance paid to individuals, which for a school generally represents financial aid.
Handle this figure carefully. A commercial service that digitises Form 990 filings reports $742,270 in grants and
assistance to individuals for the fiscal year ending June 2024. We were unable to open the filed return itself to verify that
number, so it is reported here as a third-party reading of a tax document rather than a confirmed figure. Three further
cautions: it is not a school-published aid budget and Davidson Day has never presented it as one; the fiscal year ending
June 2024 sits two years behind the 2026–27 school year this report covers; and the accompanying count of how many
individuals received assistance could not be retrieved. It should not be read as the school’s current aid budget.
TRANSPARENCY GAP — Even a percentage would need a denominator
If the school did publish a share of students on aid, that figure would need a stated base — share of total enrollment and
share of families who applied are very different numbers. There is a practical obstacle here too: published enrollment
counts for Davidson Day vary considerably across sources, from around 505 to over 570 depending on the source and
year. Any percentage would need both a base and a reliable enrollment figure to be meaningful.
Sources. davidsonday.org Tuition and Affordability page (published 9 April 2026), retrieved 22 July 2026; ProPublica Nonprofit
Explorer, EIN 11-1976223 (page updated 22 June 2026); Instrumentl Form 990 report, retrieved 22 July 2026.
All figures apply to the 2026–27 school year unless otherwise tagged. Confirm current figures with the school’s business office. 9
Davidson Day School — Financial Aid & Tuition Deep Dive Report
SECTION 5 OF 7
Merit, Scholarships and Discounts
Two named scholarships, both tied to demonstrated need — and the discounts not on record.
AT A GLANCE
Named scholarships Two: Acclaim Scholars and the Wolter Family Foundation Scholarship
Acclaim Scholars Covers 90% of tuition through graduation; Class of 2030
Wolter Family Foundation Covers all but $500 of annual tuition; Upper School
Both require A Clarity aid application and qualifying financial need
Sibling discount Not published
Employee remission Not published
Davidson Day currently names two scholarships. Both are described as requiring merit and demonstrated financial
need, which means neither is a pure merit award that sits on top of a need-based package — qualifying for
need-based assistance is a precondition for each.
Acclaim Scholars Program
Introduced to mark the school’s 25th anniversary, the Acclaim Scholars Program covers 90% of tuition through
graduation, contingent on the student remaining in good standing. It is directed at applicants in the Class of 2030.
Applicants are expected to show a strong academic profile and exemplary character, and families must complete a
Clarity financial aid application and qualify for assistance.
Wolter Family Foundation Scholarship
This scholarship covers all but $500 of annual tuition and is open to Upper School applicants who perform strongly
academically and take part in co-curricular activities. It requires strong personal recommendations and significant
demonstrated financial need, and is intended to support the recipient through graduation provided the student
remains in good standing. The scholarship is externally funded by a Cornelius-based family foundation.
TRANSPARENCY GAP — How many are awarded, and when
For both programmes, the school does not publish how many scholarships are granted each year, the selection timeline,
or renewal criteria beyond the phrase “good standing.” A family cannot tell from the public record whether these are
awarded to one student a year or to several. Enquiries go through the Director of Enrollment.
TRANSPARENCY GAP — Eligibility descriptions are inconsistent across older pages
Retired versions of the school’s aid pages, still appearing in search results, describe Acclaim Scholars as being for rising
8th-grade students for 2025–26 and the Wolter scholarship as being for rising 9th-grade students for 2025–26. The
school’s current live page describes Acclaim as being for the Class of 2030 and Wolter as being for Upper School
applicants. We have followed the current page. Families searching online should be aware that outdated eligibility
descriptions are still circulating.
All figures apply to the 2026–27 school year unless otherwise tagged. Confirm current figures with the school’s business office. 10
Davidson Day School — Financial Aid & Tuition Deep Dive Report
TRANSPARENCY GAP — Sibling, employee, military and clergy discounts
No sibling discount, military discount, or clergy discount is published. On employee families, the school operates a
separate enrollment process and an eleven-month payment plan for employee parents, but whether any tuition remission
accompanies employment is not on the public record. No indexed or sliding-scale tuition programme is published either.
Source. davidsonday.org Tuition and Affordability page (published 9 April 2026), retrieved 22 July 2026.
All figures apply to the 2026–27 school year unless otherwise tagged. Confirm current figures with the school’s business office. 11
Davidson Day School — Financial Aid & Tuition Deep Dive Report
SECTION 6 OF 7
Paying the Balance
How payment is arranged, and which contract terms stay behind the portal.
AT A GLANCE
Where terms live The Enrollment Tuition Contract, inside the family portal
Monthly plan An eleven-month plan exists
Cost of paying monthly Disclosed as $0 additional cost, in employee-facing materials
Third-party lender None named; billing is handled in-house by bank transfer
Prepayment discount Not published
Signing window Contracts to be reviewed and signed within two weeks of receipt
How enrollment and payment are set up
Both parents or guardians log into the school’s family portal under their own email addresses, review the Enrollment
Tuition Contract, select a payment option, initial to authorise drafting, and sign. Enrollment is complete once the
signed contract and the deposit are both received. The deposit is drafted immediately by bank transfer from the
account on file once the contract is submitted.
What is known about the monthly plan
The school operates an eleven-month payment plan. Its clearest public documentation appears in materials for
employee parents, which include a Truth in Lending Act disclosure stating the additional cost of the monthly plan
compared with prepaying tuition is $0. Billing is handled in-house through the business office by bank transfer; no
external tuition lender is named anywhere on the public site.
TRANSPARENCY GAP — Whether general families face the same terms
The zero-cost monthly plan disclosure appears in employee-facing material. The school does not publish an equivalent
statement for all families, so whether general families face any finance charge on a monthly plan is unconfirmed. The full
menu of payment options — whether annual, semi-annual and monthly are all offered, and on what terms — is presented
inside each family’s contract rather than published.
TRANSPARENCY GAP — The Refund Plan fee: mandatory or optional?
The fee schedule lists a Refund Plan fee at 2.8% of tuition for 2026–27 without stating whether it is required or elective.
On Upper School tuition of $26,910 that is a meaningful sum, and whether a family can decline it materially changes the
cost of attendance. The public record does not answer this.
All figures apply to the 2026–27 school year unless otherwise tagged. Confirm current figures with the school’s business office. 12
Davidson Day School — Financial Aid & Tuition Deep Dive Report
TRANSPARENCY GAP — Deposit refundability and leaving mid-year
Neither the refundability of the enrollment deposit nor a family’s financial obligation on withdrawal or mid-year departure
is published. These terms are in the Enrollment Tuition Contract, which is issued to enrolling families through the portal
and is not publicly available. Families should ask to see these clauses before signing, since they govern what happens if
plans change.
Sources. davidsonday.org enrollment instructions, employee-parent enrollment instructions and deposit instructions;
davidsonday.org Tuition and Affordability page (published 9 April 2026), retrieved 22 July 2026. All retrieved 22 July 2026.
All figures apply to the 2026–27 school year unless otherwise tagged. Confirm current figures with the school’s business office. 13
Davidson Day School — Financial Aid & Tuition Deep Dive Report
SECTION 7 OF 7
The Honest Questions
What the long-run record shows, what it cannot show, and what to ask.
AT A GLANCE
Institutional trend Seven fiscal years of public filings, FY2019 to FY2025
Revenue, FY2025 $14,700,360 (fiscal year ending June 2025)
Revenue, FY2019 $10,301,541 (fiscal year ending June 2019)
Tuition history Not retrievable; prior-year published rates were not recoverable
Full-tenure arithmetic Roughly $337,970 for a K–12 run at 2026–27 rates
The school’s public financial record
Davidson Day files an annual IRS Form 990 as a registered non-profit. These filings do not disclose tuition rates or
aid statistics, but they do show the institution’s overall financial direction. Fiscal years end in June, so each one
straddles two school years.
Fiscal year ending June Total revenue Total expenses Net assets
2019 $10,301,541 $10,347,851 $4,513,109
2020 $10,020,517 $10,174,435 $4,359,191
2021 $10,786,795 $9,495,106 $5,650,880
2022 $13,298,715 $9,998,292 $8,951,303
2023 $12,377,473 $11,400,546 $9,928,230
2024 $13,916,750 $12,497,880 $11,763,938
2025 $14,700,360 $13,997,930 $12,756,183
The FY2025 return was filed on 13 May 2026. Over this seven-year span, reported net assets rose from $4,513,109
to $12,756,183. These are institutional accounting figures, not statements about tuition or aid.
TRANSPARENCY GAP — This report cannot show you a tuition trend
We set out to publish Davidson Day’s tuition for each of the last several years so families could see the rate of change.
Prior-year versions of the tuition page could not be recovered, and the school does not publish rate history. The
current-year table overwrites the previous one. We would rather report this plainly than substitute figures from third-party
listing sites, which for this school disagree with each other and with the published table. Any family wanting to know how
quickly tuition has moved should ask the business office for the last five years of rates.
What a full run through the school costs at today’s rates
All figures apply to the 2026–27 school year unless otherwise tagged. Confirm current figures with the school’s business office. 14
Davidson Day School — Financial Aid & Tuition Deep Dive Report
The arithmetic below adds up the published 2026–27 rates for each division across the years a student would spend
in it. It is not a projection. It holds today’s prices constant across thirteen years, which will not happen — tuition is
reset annually. It also excludes every fee in Section 2. Read it as a way of seeing the scale of the published
current-year figures, not as a forecast of what anyone will pay.
Span Years At 2026–27 published rates
Kindergarten through 4th grade 5 $125,050
5th through 8th grade 4 $105,280
9th through 12th grade 4 $107,640
Kindergarten through 12th grade 13 $337,970
A student entering in 9th grade and graduating would, on the same basis, face $107,640 in published Upper School
tuition across four years at 2026–27 rates. Early Childhood years are excluded because the number of years a child
spends in that band varies.
Questions worth putting to the business office
• What share of students receive tuition assistance, and is that share of total enrollment or of families who
applied?
• What is the total aid budget this year, and what is the average award?
• Is the 2.8% Refund Plan fee required, or can we decline it?
• What is the current enrollment deposit, and under what conditions is it refundable?
• What do we owe if we withdraw mid-year?
• What do extended care, lunch, athletics team packs and arts materials cost per year?
• Are admission decisions made with or without reference to our aid application?
• What have tuition rates been for each of the last five years?
• Is there a sibling discount?
TRANSPARENCY GAP — Families above the aid threshold
Davidson Day publishes nothing about families who do not qualify for need-based assistance but for whom full tuition is a
stretch — no sliding-scale or indexed tuition programme, and no guidance aimed at that group. Its two named
scholarships both require demonstrated financial need, so neither is available to a family that does not qualify for aid.
This is a gap in what is published, and it is a common one across independent schools rather than specific to Davidson
Day.
All figures apply to the 2026–27 school year unless otherwise tagged. Confirm current figures with the school’s business office. 15
Davidson Day School — Financial Aid & Tuition Deep Dive Report
Sources and method
Every figure in this report traces to one of the sources below.
This report draws on Davidson Day School’s own published pages as the primary authority, supplemented by the
school’s public tax filings. Third-party school-listing sites were consulted only to check for discrepancies and are not
the source of any figure reported here; for this school they disagree with one another on both tuition and enrollment,
and none matched the school’s published division rates. All web sources were retrieved on 22 July 2026.
Primary — the school’s own materials
— Davidson Day School, Tuition and Affordability — the 2026–27 tuition table, the additional fee schedule, the financial aid steps and
FAQs, and both scholarship descriptions. Page published 9 April 2026.
— Davidson Day School, Enrollment Instructions and Enrollment Instructions for Employee Parents — contract flow, payment option
selection, the eleven-month plan and its Truth in Lending disclosure.
— Davidson Day School, Deposit Instructions — the $2,400 per-student deposit for 2022–23 and the immediate bank draft procedure.
— Davidson Day School, Extended Care and Back-to-School pages — care hours, age range and staffing ratio; lunch ordering;
uniform and spirit wear vendors.
— Clarity Financial Aid, Family Application Guide (2025–26 cycle), linked from the school’s aid page — the $60 submission fee and
application mechanics.
Secondary — public tax filings
— ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer, Davidson Day School, EIN 11-1976223 — Form 990 revenue, expenses and net assets for fiscal
years ending June 2019 through June 2025. Page updated 22 June 2026. The FY2025 return was filed 13 May 2026.
— Instrumentl Form 990 report, Davidson Day School — the $742,270 grants-to-individuals figure for the fiscal year ending June 2024,
reported in Section 4 with explicit caveats. This is a commercial digitisation of an IRS filing, not the filing itself, and we were unable to
verify it against the filed return.
A note on names and privacy
Individual students, families, staff and award recipients are not named anywhere in this report. Roles are referenced
where relevant. Financial aid information is inherently sensitive, and the school asks recipient families to keep
award information confidential; nothing here identifies any recipient.
A note on what this report does not do
This report does not calculate what any family would pay, does not subtract an award from a tuition figure to
produce a net price, and does not forecast future tuition. The one piece of arithmetic performed on award figures, in
Section 4, uses two numbers the school itself publishes and is labelled where it appears. Where the school
publishes a range rather than a single figure, the range is reproduced as published rather than averaged.
Before you act on anything in this report. We report only what Davidson Day publishes and what independent
research surfaced. Where a figure is not published, that is a gap in what the school discloses — not a verdict on the
school’s quality, generosity, or accessibility. Tuition and aid figures change every year, and the figures here were
retrieved in July 2026 for the 2026–27 school year. Confirm current numbers with the school’s business or admission
office before making any decision.
All figures apply to the 2026–27 school year unless otherwise tagged. Confirm current figures with the school’s business office. 16

 Snapshots were fetched with the `id_` (raw, un-rewritten) Wayback modifier and the
 tuition table was read directly out of the archived HTML.
- **Live page (current):** https://www.davidsonday.org/admission/tuition-and-affordability
- **Prior URL (through 2025–26):** https://www.davidsonday.org/admission/tuition-and-financial-aid
- **CDX queries used:**
 - `https://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=davidsonday.org/admission/tuition-and-financial-aid&output=json&from=2021&to=2026&collapse=digest`
 - `https://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=davidsonday.org/admission/tuition-and-affordability&output=json&from=2021&to=2026&collapse=digest`

**Important:** every dollar figure below was read verbatim from a retrieved archived
document. None are derived, interpolated, or back-computed.

### URL change

Through the 2025–26 year the tuition table lived at `/admission/tuition-and-financial-aid`.
For 2026–27 the school moved it to `/admission/tuition-and-affordability`. Both paths were
enumerated and fetched. This is why a single-URL Wayback query does not show the full
history.

### Band-structure change (read this before charting)

Davidson Day **restructured its early-childhood pricing** over this period, so the
early-childhood row is *not* a like-for-like series across all years:

- **2022–23 and 2023–24** — early childhood was split into several priced options:
 "Toddler (3 half days)", "Toddler (3 full days)", "Toddler (5 half days)",
 "Toddler (5 full days)", "Eaglets", and "Transitional Kindergarten". The last three of
 these shared a single full-time price.
- **2024–25** — labels changed to "Early Preschool-5 half days", "Early Preschool-5 full
 days", "Preschool (3s and 4s)", "Junior Kindergarten (4s and 5s)". The last three
 shared a single full-time price.
- **2025–26** — the half-day option disappeared from the table; "Early Preschool (2s and
 3s)", "Preschool (3s and 4s)", and "Junior Kindergarten (4s and 5s)" all shared one
 price.
- **2026–27** — collapsed into a single row: "Early Childhood (Two year olds - Junior
 Kindergarten)".

For a year-over-year chart, the **full-time early-childhood / Junior Kindergarten price**
is the correct comparable to the 2026–27 "Early Childhood" figure. That is the series
given in the main table below. The half-day and reduced-day options are preserved
separately underneath so nothing is lost.

Families receiving the 'maximum' award at Davidson Day are required to pay $3,000 per year, per student for tuition." The same $3,000 floor still appears in the 2025–26 snapshot…
sections.text:
- **Maximum award floor** — verbatim from `20240412152106`: "No financial aid award covers
 the full cost of tuition at Davidson Day School. Families receiving the 'maximum' award
 at Davidson Day are required to pay $3,000 per year, per student for tuition." The same
 $3,000 floor still appears in the 2025–26 snapshot `20250806061814`.
- **Application deadline** — February 15 each year; reapplication required annually.
- **Acclaim Scholars Program** — introduced for the class of 2030 to mark the school's 25th
 anniversary; covers 90% of tuition through graduation contingent on good standing.
 Source: 2026–27 snapshot `20260415013011`.
